Résolution.definition: The decision itself. Once adopted, it is the council's official act: it carries a number (CV-2026-0123, CE-2026-0456…) and binds the City.
Résolution.ouVousLeVoyez: This is the most common type of document on the portal.

Sommaire décisionnel.definition: The note the municipal administration writes BEFORE the decision, to explain it to elected officials: background, previous decisions, analysis of the options, recommendation, financial impact. It is the "why" behind the resolution.
Sommaire décisionnel.ouVousLeVoyez: This is the document the site's plain-language summaries are produced from — the reasoning is already written out by the City.

Procès-verbal.definition: The official record of a sitting: who was present, what was decided, and — when someone asked for it — who voted which way.
Procès-verbal.ouVousLeVoyez: It is the source of the recorded votes on the site, and the only source that gives the actual membership of each body.

Avis de motion.definition: The announcement that a by-law will be presented at a later sitting. It decides nothing: it gives notice. It is a mandatory step before adopting a by-law.
Avis de motion.ouVousLeVoyez: Often followed, a few weeks later, by the adoption of the announced by-law.

Ordonnance.definition: An implementing decision, made under a by-law already in force. It adjusts practical details without having to reopen the by-law itself.
Ordonnance.ouVousLeVoyez: Very common for parking and traffic: « Ordonnance numéro O-604 concernant des modifications aux règles portant sur le stationnement » (Order number O-604 concerning changes to the parking rules).

Règlement.definition: The most binding form of a municipal decision: a general rule that applies to everyone. Its adoption follows mandatory steps (notice of motion, draft, adoption).
Règlement.ouVousLeVoyez: The numbers tell you the body: R.V.Q. for the city, R.A.V.Q. for the agglomeration, R.C.A. for a borough.

Tableau des décisions.definition: The summary of the decisions made at a sitting, in list form.
Tableau des décisions.ouVousLeVoyez: Useful for scanning a sitting at a glance, without reading the full minutes.

Conseil municipal.definition: The 22 elected officials of Ville de Québec: the mayor and 21 councillors, one per district. It adopts by-laws, the budget, and the most important decisions.
Conseil municipal.ouVousLeVoyez: Its sittings are public and webcast, with a question period for citizens.

Comité exécutif.definition: A small group of elected officials — 9 in Québec — to whom the council has delegated a large share of its powers. It is by far the body that makes the most decisions.
Comité exécutif.ouVousLeVoyez: More than 70,000 documents on the portal come from the executive committee, compared with about 35,000 for the city council.

Conseil d'arrondissement.definition: Each of Québec's six boroughs has its own council, made up of the councillors of the districts within it. It decides local matters: neighbourhood planning, recreation, community life.
Conseil d'arrondissement.ouVousLeVoyez: The six: La Cité-Limoilou, Les Rivières, Sainte-Foy–Sillery–Cap-Rouge, Charlesbourg, Beauport, La Haute-Saint-Charles.

Commission d'urbanisme et de conservatio.equivalent: Québec City planning and conservation commission
Commission d'urbanisme et de conservatio.definition: A commission that makes binding planning decisions: architectural appearance, demolitions, heritage areas. It is chaired by elected officials, but most of its members are not elected.
Commission d'urbanisme et de conservatio.ouVousLeVoyez: A permit may depend on its opinion. It is the least known of the bodies that actually decide.

Greffier.definition: The officer who keeps the City's official documents, writes the minutes and certifies decisions. This is not an elected position.
Greffier.ouVousLeVoyez: Their signature closes the minutes, along with that of the chair of the sitting.

Conseil d'agglomération.definition: Nine seats where Québec sits with L'Ancienne-Lorette and Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, to decide on the services shared by the three cities.
Conseil d'agglomération.ouVousLeVoyez: According to the City: property assessment, public transit, arterial road network, drinking water and treatment, residual materials, public safety (police, fire, 911), municipal court, social housing and homelessness, economic development.

Ville reconstituée.aussi: de-amalgamated city · related municipality (« municipalité liée »)
Ville reconstituée.definition: A city that had been amalgamated with Québec in 2002 and regained its own existence in 2006 following a referendum. It has its own council and its own mayor. In the text of the law and in the City's documents, you more often read « municipalité liée » (related municipality) — which refers to the three cities of the agglomeration, Québec included.
Ville reconstituée.ouVousLeVoyez: Two in the Québec agglomeration: L'Ancienne-Lorette and Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures. Their elected officials vote at the agglomeration, but do not sit on Québec's city council and do not represent any Québec district.

Compétence d'agglomération.definition: A field that the law assigns to the agglomeration council rather than to each city separately, because the service is shared. The rest — what are called local jurisdictions (« compétences de proximité ») — remains with each city.
Compétence d'agglomération.ouVousLeVoyez: This is why an elected official from another city votes on matters that affect Québec.

Demander le vote.definition: To require that the votes be counted one by one. Without this request, a decision is adopted without a roll call and no one is named in the minutes.
Demander le vote.ouVousLeVoyez: This is the key to the site's vote registry: the only votes we know in detail are those that someone called for.

Adoptée à l'unanimité.ouVousLeVoyez: The most common wording, because most decisions pass without opposition.

Adoptée à la majorité.definition: Adopted, but at least one person voted against. The minutes then name who.
Adoptée à la majorité.ouVousLeVoyez: This is the case for almost all of the recorded votes on the site.

Adoptée sur division.definition: Adopted despite a recorded opposition, without the votes necessarily having been counted by name.
Adoptée sur division.ouVousLeVoyez: Rarer than « à la majorité » (by majority), and less informative: we know there was disagreement, but not always from whom.

Prise d’acte.definition: The council officially notes that a document has been presented to it. This does not approve it: it records it.
Prise d’acte.ouVousLeVoyez: Often for reports, agreements already signed, or mandatory filings.

Mairesse suppléante.definition: The elected official designated to replace the mayor when the mayor is absent or unable to act.
Mairesse suppléante.ouVousLeVoyez: At the 2026 agglomeration sittings, the mayor of Québec was replaced at each of the twelve sittings.

Dérogation mineure.definition: Permission to depart slightly from a zoning rule for a specific lot — a setback, a height, a number of parking spaces — without changing the by-law for everyone.
Dérogation mineure.ouVousLeVoyez: Almost always tied to a specific address, which is named in the subject of the decision.

Plan d'implantation et d'intégration arc.equivalent: Site planning and architectural integration programme
Plan d'implantation et d'intégration arc.definition: A mechanism that submits a project to an assessment of its appearance and how it fits into its surroundings, beyond the numerical rules of zoning.
Plan d'implantation et d'intégration arc.ouVousLeVoyez: This is often what brings a file before the Commission d'urbanisme (planning commission). The City's vocabulary changed along the way: the acronym with periods, « P.I.I.A. », appears in 4,352 documents, mostly between 2006 and 2017, then disappears in favour of the full wording.

Zonage.definition: The division of the territory into zones, each with rules on what may be built and done there.
Zonage.ouVousLeVoyez: Québec's zoning grid is published as open data.

Adjudication.definition: The official awarding of a contract to a bidder, at the end of a call for tenders.
Adjudication.ouVousLeVoyez: « Adjudication d'un contrat pour… » (Awarding of a contract for…) is one of the most frequent wordings on the portal.

Appel d'offres.definition: The mandatory competitive process before awarding a contract above a certain amount. A public call is open to all; an invitational call is limited to suppliers that have been approached.
Appel d'offres.ouVousLeVoyez: Municipal contracts are published on SEAO, Québec's electronic tendering system.

Gré à gré.definition: A contract entered into directly, without a competitive process. The law allows it only in specific cases.
Gré à gré.ouVousLeVoyez: Also appears for property acquisitions: « de gré à gré ou par expropriation » (by mutual agreement or by expropriation).

Appropriation.definition: Setting aside an amount already available for a specific expense. It is not new borrowing.
Appropriation.ouVousLeVoyez: « Appropriation d'un montant de 2 510 000 $ à même le fonds général » (Appropriation of an amount of $2,510,000 from the general fund).

Règlement d'emprunt.definition: The by-law by which the City authorizes itself to borrow in order to finance a project, generally a long-term investment.
Règlement d'emprunt.ouVousLeVoyez: It specifies the amount and the repayment period.

Expropriation.definition: The forced acquisition of land or of a right by the City for a public purpose, with compensation to the owner.
Expropriation.ouVousLeVoyez: Often followed by a « règlement hors tribunal » (out-of-court settlement), that is, an agreement on the compensation without going before a judge.
